questions.stem: A straight line has equation $y = 3x - 4$. State (a) the gradient of the line and (b) the $y$-intercept of the line.
questions.modelAnswer: The equation is in the form $y = mx + c$, where $m$ is the gradient and $c$ is the $y$-intercept. Comparing $y = 3x - 4$ with $y = mx + c$: the gradient is $3$ and the $y$-intercept is $-4$, so the line crosses the $y$-axis at $(0, -4)$.

questions.stem: A circle has radius $5$ cm. Work out its circumference, leaving your answer in terms of $\pi$.
questions.modelAnswer: Circumference $= 2\pi r = 2 \times \pi \times 5 = 10\pi$. Answer: $10\pi$ cm (about $31.4$ cm if evaluated).

questions.stem: The $n$th term of a sequence is $5n - 2$. Write down the first three terms of the sequence.
markscheme: B1: first two terms correct: $3$ and $8$
questions.modelAnswer: Substitute $n = 1, 2, 3$ into $5n - 2$: $5(1) - 2 = 3$, $5(2) - 2 = 8$ and $5(3) - 2 = 13$. The first three terms are $3, 8, 13$ (each term is $5$ more than the previous one, matching the common difference $5$).

questions.stem: A train travels $180$ km in $2$ hours. (a) Calculate its average speed in km/h. (b) Convert this speed into m/s.
questions.modelAnswer: (a) Average speed $= \dfrac{180}{2} = 90$ km/h. (b) In $1$ hour the train covers $90\,000$ m, and $1$ hour is $3600$ s, so the speed is $\dfrac{90\,000}{3600} = 25$ m/s. Answers: $90$ km/h and $25$ m/s.

questions.stem: The table shows the scores of $10$ students in a quiz. Score $1$: frequency $3$; score $2$: frequency $4$; score $3$: frequency $2$; score $4$: frequency $1$. Calculate the mean score.
markscheme: M1: divides by the total frequency, $10$
questions.modelAnswer: Multiply each score by its frequency: $1 \times 3 = 3$, $2 \times 4 = 8$, $3 \times 2 = 6$ and $4 \times 1 = 4$. The total of all scores is $3 + 8 + 6 + 4 = 21$. Divide by the number of students: $\dfrac{21}{10} = 2.1$. The mean score is $2.1$.

questions.stem: Rectangle A measures $6$ cm by $4$ cm. Rectangle B is mathematically similar to rectangle A, and its shorter side is $10$ cm. Work out the length of the longer side of rectangle B.
questions.modelAnswer: Similar shapes have corresponding sides in the same ratio. The shorter sides correspond: scale factor $= \dfrac{10}{4} = 2.5$. So the longer side of rectangle B is $6 \times 2.5 = 15$ cm. Check: $\dfrac{10}{4} = \dfrac{15}{6} = 2.5$ ✓

questions.stem: Work out $(3 \times 10^{4}) \times (2 \times 10^{5})$, giving your answer in standard form.
markscheme: M1: multiplies the numbers and adds the powers of ten: $6 \times 10^{4+5}$
questions.modelAnswer: Multiply the number parts and the powers of ten separately: $(3 \times 2) \times (10^{4} \times 10^{5}) = 6 \times 10^{4+5} = 6 \times 10^{9}$. Since $6$ lies between $1$ and $10$, this is already in standard form.

questions.stem: A semicircle has radius $4$ cm. (a) Work out the length of its curved edge. (b) Work out its area. Leave both answers in terms of $\pi$.
markscheme: M1: curved edge $=$ half a circumference, $\dfrac{2 \times \pi \times 4}{2}$ or $\pi \times 4$
questions.modelAnswer: (a) The curved edge is half the circumference of the full circle: $\dfrac{2\pi r}{2} = \pi r = 4\pi$ cm. (b) The area is half the area of the full circle: $\dfrac{\pi r^{2}}{2} = \dfrac{\pi \times 16}{2} = 8\pi$ cm$^{2}$. Answers: $4\pi$ cm and $8\pi$ cm$^{2}$.
